::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 26th 1895  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne  
**Manuscript:** MS Oriel College, Oxford
:::

Dear [Miss Hale](people/person_605.qmd)
Thank you for your very interesting letter.  I am amused at what you say of [Mr Keble](people/person_798.qmd) calling his father the Governor.[^1]  I should think it was a domestic name, invented before the slang term arose.  I know the family were fond, in their old Fairford days- of pet nicknames and that J K himself was called by his sisters ‘Charles’ for no reason that their friends the Dysons could trace.  I knew all the family like relations after they were at Hursley and especially loved [Miss Elizabeth Keble](people/person_796.qmd).

yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The *OED* has citations of *governor* 7b *colloq*. ‘applied by young men to their fathers’ from 1827, which suggests that CMY may have been mistaken in thinking Keble (b. 1792) could not have used it in that sense.
